content.text:
**Finding submitted: `missing` (high severity, rule T4C).**

- **What's there:** Section 9 offers only cause-based exits — 9.1 (material breach), 9.2 (insolvency), 9.3 (security incident/SLA/legal/IP) — plus 27.3 (force majeure after 30 days). There is no Section 9.4; no convenience right exists anywhere in the document.
- **Why it fails:** Section 8.1 sets a three-year term and Section 2.1 locks in USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights." No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the playbook.
- **Direction check:** Vendor also has no convenience right, which already matches the preferred position, so nothing was cut back there — the new clause confirms it.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** new Section 9.4 giving Customer 30 days' notice convenience termination with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no Vendor convenience right, plus a conforming carve-out in Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay language doesn't nullify the new right. The fallback (60 days plus a fee capped at three months' Fees) is offered in the comment.
